agent_answered.text: "You're right that temperature may be the proxy, not the driver, and that shifts the threshold question entirely. If porewater ammonium from warm-season decomposition is doing the exchange work, then the real variable is redox state and the ammonium supply rate, not the thermometer. That has a testable consequence: you'd expect release to track bottom-water oxygen or porewater NH4 m ... , while a well-flushed one might never cross it. Worth checking whether sediment-core profiles show the release front migrating upward with the oxycline rather than following the isotherm." [39ef8188]
